frame: X along the existing rotating center axle, Y up from floor, Z fore/aft. Nominal bearing axis Y104, Z0.

expansion_pilots.status: Two smooth blind pilot bores only, reserved for future printed expansion screws. No threads, expansion screws or clips are modeled. Pads have 2 mm radial and blind-end walls.

axle.interface: 608 journals on the printed spindle (cad/spindle.py). The drive journal key and clip groove match the printed disc and clip; the thrust sleeves stop 0.2 mm short of each inner race.
axle.left_journal_note: Left journal is a printed slip fit (Ø7.9 against the 608 Ø8 bore) so the left 608 slides off for spool changes; the allowance needs a physical trial. The right journal keeps the nominal Ø8 with the disc key and clip groove.

magnets.note: Shared magnet spec and cup for the disc and the outside handwheel (cad/wheel.py reads it): purchased 15 x 3 mm axially magnetized discs.

material: Bambu PLA Basic is a prior prototype material; no manufacturing settings or fabrication are approved for this concept.
provenance: 16 November 2026: founder requested removing the redundant rounded wall noses and auditing each printed part for print preparation. Rounded noses and their purpose-free support wings are removed; the surrounding guard lip retains the same drive-wall plane and nominal 1.5 mm gap. Both purchased 608 bearings, four printed parts, 82.2 mm wall span and 75 × 130 mm base are retained. Fabrication-mesh audit found a zero-thickness tangent rib/air-tube contact; rib inner radius reduced from 21 to 20.8 mm for positive overlap, preserving the Ø6 air bore and outside footprint. Later 16 November: a narrow guard roof with 1:1 axial growth and 35 degree side-strut sections lands on the existing legs, replacing guard scaffolding. The roof stops 0.2 mm inside the wall plane, preserving its contact face. Free diaphragm tips are capped at the existing guard-contact height. Bearing seats, base and inboard chamber-growth space are retained; comparative linear stiffness and actual slices bound this optimization. Physical qualification remains outstanding. 17 November 2026: frame replaced by the founder-directed spoked U-rim (two upper spokes, R6 junction rounds, central brace, three 45-degree rim undersides); fixed inboard bearing heads replaced by keyed seats for two removable carriers that lift out with the high-flow cartridge; the green axle/core is superseded by that cartridge. 17 November 2026: founder replaced the high-flow cartridge with a lighter printed spindle and threaded collar that clamp the spool by its bore-end chamfers; the journals, disc key and clip groove are unchanged. Independent review the same day: cone rings lengthened inboard to 3.5 mm with struts joining the full ring section, arms deepened to 6 mm, cones shortened to keep running gaps through the ±0.5 mm axial float, left journal made a Ø7.9 slip fit for spool changes Later the same day the founder required the collar to hold in both turning directions, so an integral positive collar lock (crest slots on the spindle, compliant key on the collar) replaced the thread-hand requirement.
limitations: Seven printed holder parts (frame, two removable carriers, spindle, collar, disc, clip) plus two purchased 608s.
Carriers seat by gravity only; no latch. Guide strength, carrier retention, alignment and bearing grip are unqualified.
C-seat entry requires nominal 0.2 mm jaw movement per side; clip entry requires nominal 0.1 mm per jaw. Snap force, stress, fatigue and creep remain unqualified.

The spindle and collar cones are sized to the bore-end chamfers of Bambu's published printable spool model; seat and clamp on actual molded spools are unverified, as are printed thread fit and clamp torque.
Bottom-side desiccant baskets remain to be designed.
Base pilot holes reserve space for future printed expansion screws only. No thread or expansion screw is modeled.
The magnet pocket is 3.9 mm deep for a nominal 3 mm magnet with a 1.3 mm front cover. Coupling torque and adhesive retention are untested.

carriers.status: Removable keyed carriers; frame tongue runs in carrier grooves. Gravity seating only, no latch. Guide strength, retention and bearing grip unqualified.

spindle.status: Third candidate. Unprinted and unqualified: thread fit, collar lock, clamp torque, strength, left-journal slip fit and print orientation are untested.
spindle.boss_ramp_note: Conical ramp from the thread boss inboard face down to the shaft, angle measured from the axle, so the boss face needs no support when the spindle prints refill end up.
spindle.seat_note: Each 45-degree cone seats in a spool bore-end chamfer (bore R27.5, chamfer from |X|32.9 at R27.5 to |X|33.7 at R28.3, hub faces at |X|33.7), taken from the Bambu printable reference spool model. Molded Bambu spool dimensions are unmeasured; the collar travel absorbs hub-width differences.

thread.note: Custom printed thread (Ø18 major, 3 mm pitch, truncated 60-degree tooth) shared by spindle and collar only; not an ISO M18 nut fit. The hand does not matter for retention: the collar lock holds it in both directions.

spindle.running_gap_note: min_running_gap is the gap that must remain after the rotating unit takes up its full axial float (thrust-sleeve gap + 608 seat clearance + carrier tongue/groove play, derived in stand.py).

lock.purpose: Positive collar retention in both turning directions: a key on a compliant arm in the collar wall drops into one of the crest-only slots along the spindle thread; lift the paddle to turn the collar.
lock.status: Unprinted: arm strain, lift feel, key/slot wear and stop strength need a physical trial.
